trial_court: Family Court, Agartala, West Tripura in Title Suit (Nullity) No.138 of 2007
case_name: Sri Rupak Kumar Acharjee vs Smti Antara Nandi(Shil)

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Sri Rupak Kumar Acharjee, second husband of respondent No.1
parties.respondent_defendant: Smti Antara Nandi(Shil), respondent No.2 (first husband) and Sri Dipan Shil, respondent No.2

facts_of_case: Petitioner is the second husband of respondent No.1, who had previously married respondent No.2 and obtained a certificate of marriage on 12-1-2007. Respondent No.1 entered into marriage with petitioner without disclosing her previous marriage. Petitioner seeks to question the validity of the judgment declaring the first marriage as null and void.

legal_principles.principle: In divorce proceedings, the Court must satisfy itself that the petition is not presented or prosecuted in collusion with the respondent.
legal_principles.held: Thus, it is obvious that in divorce proceedings, the Court must, inter alia, satisfy itself that the petition is not presented or prosecuted in collusion with the respondent.

legal_principles.principle: The Court granting a decree of divorce must make a brief reference to the circumstances, on which it believes that the petition is not inspired by collusion between the parties.
legal_principles.held: It is appropriate that the Court granting a decree of divorce must make a brief reference to the circumstances, on which it believes that the petition is not inspired by collusion between the parties.

outcome.final_order: The court sets aside the judgment of the trial court and holds that the first marriage was not null and void. The certificate of marriage obtained by respondents is declared operative and valid.
